newsitem.title: KENYA: Typhus epidemics sweep camps in Burundi, WHO.
newsitem.headline: Typhus epidemics sweep camps in Burundi, WHO.

text.p: Typhus epidemics are sweeping through camps in four provinces of Burundi for displaced and "regrouped" people, the U.N. World Health Organisation (WHO) said on Friday.
Bernard Lala, WHO representative in Burundi, told Reuters the typhus rate soared in October when troops began "regrouping" villagers in camps, officially to protect them from Hutu rebels.

"Now we are talking about epidemics in the four provinces of Kayanza, Muramvya, rural Bujumbura and Gitega...We also have a high rate of dead from typhus because people are already weakened by malnutrition," said Lala, who is visiting Nairobi.
He said an estimated 400,000 to 500,000 people -- mainly of the Tutsi minority -- who were displaced by fighting in the last three years lived in camps protected by the army in Burundi.
In addition 200,000 Tutsis and Hutus had been regrouped in camps in three provinces by the army since October, he added.
U.N. human rights monitors say troops forced the mainly Hutu peasants out of their homes in the hills and into the camps.
"The conditions are the same: a lack of basic sanitation, poor water and hygenic conditions and not enough food," said Lala. The World Food Programme is supplying the regroupment camps.
Typhus is an infectious fever that leads to delirium. It is usually transmitted by lice, which are common in the camps.
Lala said regional sanctions against Burundi imposed shortly after a coup by the Tutsi-dominated army last July were delaying the delivery of insecticides to aid agencies to kill the lice.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and a civil war between the army and Hutu rebels since the killing of Burundis first freely-elected Hutu president in October 1993.
